questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Biodiversity and its Importance' refers to.
questions.a: Biodiversity refers to the variety of plant and animal life in a particular habitat or in the world as a whole, including genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Biodiversity and its Importance'.
questions.a: Biodiversity is the foundation of healthy ecosystems and is essential for ecological stability, human survival, and economic development.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Biodiversity and its Importance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Introduction

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Flora and Fauna in India' refers to.
questions.a: India is one of the world's richest countries in terms of biological diversity, with over 81,000 species of fauna and 47,000 species of flora, owing to its varied climate and topography.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Flora and Fauna in India'.
questions.a: India's rich biodiversity is a result of diverse climatic and geographical conditions supporting a wide range of plant and animal species.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Flora and Fauna in India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Flora and Fauna in India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Classification of Species' refers to.
questions.a: Species are classified as normal, endangered, vulnerable, rare, and endemic based on their population status and risk of extinction.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Classification of Species'.
questions.a: Classification of species helps prioritise conservation efforts by identifying those most at risk of extinction.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Classification of Species' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Classification of Species

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Conservation of Forest and Wildlife' refers to.
questions.a: Conservation of forest and wildlife involves protection, preservation, and sustainable management of natural resources to maintain ecological balance and prevent species extinction.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Conservation of Forest and Wildlife'.
questions.a: Conservation is essential to preserve biodiversity, maintain ecological balance, and ensure sustainable use of natural resources for future generations.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Conservation of Forest and Wildlife' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Conservation of Forest and Wildlife in India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Project Tiger' refers to.
questions.a: Project Tiger is a wildlife conservation initiative launched by the Government of India in 1973 to protect the Bengal tiger from extinction and to preserve its habitat.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Project Tiger'.
questions.a: Project Tiger was launched to protect the endangered Bengal tiger and its habitat through tiger reserves across India.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Project Tiger' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Project Tiger

concepts.title: Types and Distribution of Forests in India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types and Distribution of Forests in India' refers to.
questions.a: India's forests are classified into reserved, protected, and unclassed forests based on legal status, and into tropical evergreen, tropical deciduous, thorn, montane, and mangrove forests based on climate and vegetation type.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types and Distribution of Forests in India'.
questions.a: India has diverse forest types distributed according to climate, rainfall, and soil, classified legally and ecologically for management.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Types and Distribution of Forests in India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types and Distribution of Forests

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Community and Conservation' refers to.
questions.a: Community conservation involves local communities in the protection and management of forests and wildlife, recognising their traditional knowledge and dependence on natural resources.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Community and Conservation'.
questions.a: Community participation is crucial for effective conservation, as local people have traditional knowledge and a stake in sustainable resource use.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Community and Conservation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Community and Conservation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sacred Groves' refers to.
questions.a: Sacred groves are patches of forest or trees that are protected by local communities for religious and cultural reasons, preserving biodiversity in its pristine form.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sacred Groves'.
questions.a: Sacred groves are nature's sanctuaries protected by communities for religious and cultural beliefs, preserving rare and endemic species.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sacred Groves' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Community and Conservation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Deforestation and its Causes' refers to.
questions.a: Deforestation is the clearing of forests for non-forest uses such as agriculture, mining, and urbanisation, leading to loss of biodiversity and ecological imbalance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Deforestation and its Causes'.
questions.a: Deforestation is the permanent destruction of forests for alternative land use, causing biodiversity loss, soil erosion, and climate change.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Deforestation and its Causes' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Deforestation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Conservation Efforts and Legal Framework' refers to.
questions.a: India has enacted several laws and policies for forest and wildlife conservation, including the Indian Wildlife Protection Act 1972, the Forest Conservation Act 1980, and the National Forest Policy 1988.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Conservation Efforts and Legal Framework'.
questions.a: Legal and policy frameworks in India provide the foundation for forest and wildlife conservation through legislation and institutional mechanisms.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Conservation Efforts and Legal Framework' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Conservation of Forest and Wildlife in India
